newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine starts trading band 1.70-90 hryvnias/dlr.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine starts trading band 1.70-90 hryvnias/dlr.

text.p: Ukraine has announced a currency corridor, or trading band, of 1.70 to 1.90 hryvnias against the dollar to take effect today until at least the end of 1997, Ukraine's economic policy chief said on Friday.

"Today we can say that we will maintain a single rate with the central bank which will be implemented at 1.80, plus or minus 10 points, therefore from 1.70 to 1.90." Deputy Prime Minister Serhiy Tyhypko told reporters. "It's effective today until the end of the year."

"This will give a certain stability to Ukrainian producers and to investors who work on the Treasury bill market, and it will also be easier for the government to make budget calculations," he said of the currency which was introduced last September.

Tyhypko said the move had the support of the International Monetary Fund, which completed a week of meetings on Friday to review Ukraine's progress on the long-delayed budget -- set to pave the way for a multi-billion dollar credit.
"The main thing for the government is to maintain currency stability, but it also needs to look after exporters," he said.
The Ukraine authorities, which forecast inflation this year at 25 percent down from 39.7 percent in 1996, have been talking of announcing a trading band for the hryvnia since its introduction.
